content.rationale: Ownership is the boundary every guard checks — recording, removal and undo all attribute file state through it — so it is derived from a change's own already-loaded document and nothing else, never by scanning: its node file, named through store_path so there is one layout, plus the paths its content.ref lists when ref is an array; an inline ref yields the node file alone. Each listed path is read as a repo-relative path in normal form, so a leading `./` and repeated `/` separators do not distinguish paths: the owned set holds one entry per file under one spelling, which is what lets a guard compare files rather than typed strings. `..` belongs to that normal form because it still says where a name sits: each `..` is folded against the ordinary component before it, so `src/../src/x.rs` and `src/x.rs` name one file and `a/b/../c` names `a/c`, and a `..` that survives that folding has nothing left in the repository to name — it points outside — so that listed path contributes no owned path at all, rather than an entry no guard could compare against a file. A path whose components all fold away names the repository root, which is inside the repository and not an escape, so it keeps the one spelling `.` a lone `.` already has instead of being dropped. Absolute paths, symlinks and case are out of scope, as before. The document is the crate's serde_json `Value`, so the module is written against serde and serde_json alone.
